_comment: Frequently asked questions. Hand-edited. Answers must match data/practical.json and the agreed registration rules — change both together. Links in answers are written as {label|url} and rendered as anchors.

items.q: When and where is Energy Planning Week 2026?
items.a: 1–4 December 2026 at the GIZ Campus Forum, Friedrich-Ebert-Allee 32, 53113 Bonn, Germany. The Week runs in a hybrid format: on site in Bonn and online through Microsoft Teams. All times are CET.

The Week is designed primarily for government energy planners and policymakers, alongside representatives of the energy industry, financial institutions, regulators, utilities, intergovernmental organisations and the scientific and modelling community. Anyone interested is welcome to follow the sessions online.

items.q: Can I register to attend in Bonn?
items.a: Registration is currently open for online participation only. On-site places (up to 120) are confirmed directly by the co-hosts, with priority for speakers, government planners, and members and partners of the LTES Network, GCEP and GET.transform.
Complete the {registration form|https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/UhjVrHEPrx} to join online. Connection details (Microsoft Teams) are shared with registered online participants ahead of the event.

items.q: I need a visa to travel to Germany. What should I do?
items.a: Apply as early as possible: Schengen visa appointments in some countries are booked months ahead. If you are attending in person, IRENA can provide a visa support letter on request; contact {LTES@irena.org|mailto:LTES@irena.org}. Passport details are requested separately, and only once your place is confirmed. Please do not send them by email.

items.q: How do I get to the venue?
items.a: From Bonn Central Station (Bonn Hbf), take underground tram (U-Bahn) line 16 or 63 towards Bad Godesberg, or line 66 towards Bad Honnef, and get off at Ollenhauerstraße. Turn right onto Friedrich-Ebert-Allee and walk towards the city centre; GIZ is on the left. From Cologne Bonn or Frankfurt airport, trains and buses run to Bonn Hbf ({bahn.com|https://www.bahn.com/en}). Local fares are paid by participants.

items.q: What do I need to bring on the first day?
items.a: Registration and badge collection open at 08:00 on Tuesday 1 December at the GIZ Campus. Bring a valid photo ID (passport or national identity card). Your badge is needed to enter the venue all week, and you will be asked to sign a photography consent form when you collect it.

Yes, for registered on-site participants: breakfast, coffee breaks and a vegetarian lunch (with a vegan option) on all four days, a vegetarian welcome dinner on Tuesday 1 December (19:00–21:00, Eventmanufaktur, near Bonn Hbf) and a reception after Day 3. Please send any dietary restrictions to {LTES@irena.org|mailto:LTES@irena.org} as soon as possible.

items.q: Do I book my own accommodation?
items.a: Yes, unless your accommodation is covered by other means. Hotels in the Bundesviertel or near Bonn Hbf give the easiest access to the venue.

items.q: Can I follow the Week online?
items.a: Yes. All plenary and numbered sessions are streamed on Microsoft Teams, except the closed-door LTES Network strategic meeting on Day 2. Connection details are shared with registered online participants ahead of the event.

items.q: What language are the sessions in?
Who do I contact with questions?
items.a: Write to the LTES Network at {LTES@irena.org|mailto:LTES@irena.org}.
